transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-25
Start: 08:34 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tom (Redwood SE), Jasmin (CSM), Alex (Sunset Dock CTO), Rina (Head of ML), Owen (DevOps), Marta (Product), Samir (Security)

Summary:
Quick first-week onboarding standup to align runbook, staging access, and initial pilot scope. Focus areas: VPC/staging networking, SSO, telemetry/observability, latency baseline, and data retention/KMS. Action items and next steps agreed.

Topics:
- Staging access and network routing (VPC peering, FRR)
- SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping
- Pilot definition (traffic volume, models, success criteria)
- Benchmarks: latency, throughput, token cost targets
- Security: logs, KMS, audit retention

Action Items (recap):
- See metadata action_items above

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, this is Maya from Redwood, we'll keep this tight 45-ish minutes, but looks like we have 52 on the calendar so good.
[00:12] Alex: Yep thanks - appreciate it. We wanted to make sure the first week things are unblocked, Rina kicked off some model mapping yesterday.
[00:20] Rina: yeah hi, quick thing, we're planning to run two flavors of workloads, a user-facing chat flow and an internal vector search enrichment pipeline. so we need embeddings and chat endpoints.
[00:33] Tom: cool, for embeddings we can use the hosted endpoint initially, get you up with API keys, then the dedicated pool for steady traffic — we can advise quant profiles for cost.
[00:45] Owen: we want to test VPC/private first week, is that doable? We need to know if Redwood Private will run in our VPC or if it's a managed peering.
[00:55] Jasmin: Good question — typically we do two patterns: managed peering (fast) or full private install (longer lead). For a pilot we recommend VPC peering into a staging subnet so you can validate networking and RBAC.
[01:10] Samir: how do you handle KMS? Our compliance team requires keys to be customer-managed.
[01:16] Priya Kaur: we support customer KMS via our integrations, can plug into AWS KMS or GCP KMS, and HSM for enterprise. we'll need the key arn and access role.
[01:28] Samir: ok, good. we'll put that in the action items.
[01:33] Marta: who owns the playbook? which doc do we follow for the staging handoff?
[01:38] Elliot: I'll drop the onboarding runbook link in the notes — it's the living doc. It has the staging checklist and common gotchas (firewall ports, NACLs, certs).
[01:50] Maya: great — quick run-through of the pilot scope: 1) Validate connectivity and authentication; 2) Run a synthetic latency baseline at expected RPS; 3) Monitor cost per 1k tokens for the embeddings workload; 4) Establish alerting and tracing in Console. Does that align?
[02:10] Alex: yes, though for cost we want ballpark per-1M tokens since our budget is tight.
[02:16] Tom: sure — we'll run a small baseline and extrapolate; note that quantization changes and batching can shift numbers. also prefix caching (we call K-V cache in docs) can reduce tokens for chat flows.
[02:30] Rina: small nit - in your docs you mention KV cash in one place, is that the same as KV cache?
[02:34] Tom: ha, yes that's a known transcription typo in some exports, K-V cache, not K-V cash.
[02:41] Owen: Networking — we did a quick check, our infra team prefers VPC peering with an AWS Transit gateway. can Redwood support that pattern?
[02:50] Priya Kaur: yes transit-gw peering is supported, we just need the CIDR ranges and expected NAT egress. we'll also share our recommended SG and port lists.
[03:05] Samir: audit logs — retention? we need 12 months immutably.
[03:10] Jasmin: Our observability plan includes per-route logs sent to your S3/logging endpoint; retention policies are configurable. for immutability we'll need to coordinate S3 bucket policies.
[03:22] Samir: perfect.
[03:25] [04:00] Marta: can we map product roles? e.g., who will be our day-to-day contact for incidents?
[04:05] Jasmin: day-to-day is me (CSM), for seeding infra and perf Tom will lead, and Maya is your AE for contractual/questions.
[04:14] Alex: sounds good.
[04:18] [06:00] Tom: on the latency baseline — can you share a typical prompt size distribution and expected concurrency? if you have p95 goals that's super helpful.
[06:25] Owen: we expect bursts to 150 RPS for chat during morning peak; avg prompt ~300 tokens, response 150 tokens. target p95 under 250ms for short queries, 800ms for longer ones.
[06:40] Tom: ok that's helpful; hosted might meet those p95 numbers for small prompts, but longer sequences and KV cache warmup will affect p95. we'll run an initial hosted baseline, and if needed propose Dedicated nodes with specified batch tuning.
[06:58] Rina: question on model versions — do you pin model versions for the pilot? we want deterministic outputs across runs.
[07:06] Priya Kaur: yes you can pin model versions; Redwood supports version pinning and rollout policies. in Dedicated you can freeze a model binary, in hosted we provide model tags and compatibility.
[07:20] Alex: any known gotchas with our stack? We're using EKS with Istio sidecars.
[07:26] Tom: Istio is fine, just be mindful of mTLS policies that might block mutual TLS when peering; also check egress rules for streaming responses. we've seen sidecar timeouts cause truncated streams.
[07:40] Owen: noted. We'll validate with a quick curl from a staging pod.
[07:45] [12:00] Marta: observability — can we mirror traces into our Datadog?
[12:06] Elliot: yes traces and metrics can be exported to Datadog; Console also provides token-level cost breakdowns we can send as a CSV for your finance team.
[12:17] Marta: nice.
[12:20] [15:00] Samir: security review — do you support SAML group-to-role mapping? and SCIM?
[15:08] Jasmin: yes SAML & SCIM supported. we map SAML attributes to RBAC roles, and SCIM for user provisioning. we'll request SAML metadata file and SCIM endpoint details.
[15:24] Samir: we also need encryption in transit assurance and algorithm details.
[15:29] Priya Kaur: TLS1.3, mutual TLS where required, and we can share our crypto spec. we'll attach it to the runbook.
[15:40] [20:00] Alex: timeline — what's realistic for getting a staging pilot live?
[20:08] Maya: for a VPC peering pilot with hosted model access we can be live in 7-10 business days if keys/certs and traffic spec are provided quickly. Dedicated/private installs add 3-6 weeks depending on capacity scheduling.
[20:26] Alex: ok we'll aim for the faster path first.
[20:30] [24:00] Tom: Benchmarks — I'll run two baselines: 1) hosted small concurrency; 2) hosted with simulated token lengths matching your profile. I'll include per-token cost and p95 numbers.
[24:12] Rina: please include how batching and quant profiles affect latency vs cost in the report.
[24:18] Tom: yes will include a small section on tradeoffs, quant-8 vs quant-4 and recommended batch sizes for 150 RPS.
[24:30] [28:00] Owen: access — what's the minimal set of firewall openings? we want only necessary ports.
[28:08] Priya Kaur: we'll provide a minimal SG set: outbound HTTPS (443) to our egress endpoints, plus optional SSH for jumpbox if you want a bastion. in peering model, internal TCP ranges for control plane. We'll paste exact CIDRs in the runbook.
[28:35] Owen: perfect.
[28:40] [32:00] Marta: product question: how will fallback work if dedicated nodes hit capacity?
[32:12] Maya: Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants in different capacity tiers; that's in the rollout policy. we can test canary and fallback behavior during pilot.
[32:28] Rina: will fallback change output characteristics? we need to ensure functional parity.
[32:35] Tom: fallbacks may use a model variant with different tokenization/quant; we'll document differences and include acceptance checks in the pilot test suite.
[32:50] [36:00] Alex: billing — can we get a rough estimate for 1 month of pilot at 150 RPS and embeddings?
[36:08] Maya: we'll do an extrapolated cost in the runbook based on baseline results; again quant and batching matter. expect a preliminary estimate within 48 hours after the baseline run.
[36:25] [40:00] Jasmin: Recap of next actions: Maya to share runbook and checklist; Tom to run baselines; Owen to share traffic and egress specs; Samir to confirm compliance/KMS needs; Rina to confirm pinned models and acceptance criteria.
[40:43] Alex: sounds good.
[40:46] [45:00] Marta: small ask — could we get a one-pager describing the dev-to-prod path? our PMs want a digest.
[45:10] Elliot: yes — one-pager with staging->canary->prod steps, roles, and SLAs; I'll attach to the runbook.
[45:22] Maya: final — schedule benchmark review next Wednesday, 30 minutes with Tom and Owen. I'll send calendar invite.
[45:34] Alex: great thanks all.
[45:36] [51:00] Maya: thanks everyone, end of meeting.

Shared links and notes:
- Onboarding runbook (Elliot to share) - link placeholder: https://redwood.app/runbooks/sunset-dock-onboard
- Baseline template (Tom) - will be uploaded to the runbook
- Security checklist (Jasmin) - attachment in follow-up email

End of transcript.
